patch_description: The current algorithm computes a shortest path independently for each destination, ignoring that many destinations may share the same low-cost egress links. This causes redundant expensive transfers on parallel/identical routes. A better strategy: process destinations in order, and once an edge has been used by a previous destination's path, discount its effective cost (near zero) for subsequent route searches. This encourages later destinations to reuse already-paid-for links, producing a Steiner-tree-like broadcast structure that substantially reduces total transfer cost, while still guaranteeing each destination remains reachable. We use per-destination copies of the graph weights so the original graph G is untouched, and all num_partitions per destination are still populated exactly as before so the topology format stays compatible.
